subject: SimNIBS example subject Ernie
binaryCountConvention: count is the number of scalar typed-array elements

coordinateSystem.name: SimNIBS world coordinates in subject space
coordinateSystem.bakedTransform: none except mm-to-m conversion and float32 rounding
coordinateSystem.optionalYUpFormula: x = raw_x - center_x; y = raw_z - center_z; z = -(raw_y - center_y); optional only, not baked
coordinateSystem.zUpViewer: Use camera.up=(0,0,1); same scene scale and transform for both buffers

source.originalCoordinates: Original float64 millimetre node coordinates remain unchanged in the source .msh

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International
license.attribution: Derived from SimNIBS example dataset v4.1, Ernie head model. © SimNIBS developers 2024. CC BY-NC 4.0.
license.modifications: Selected one scalp and one gray-matter connected component; compacted indices; converted mm to m; float32 coordinates; computed and quantized vertex normals. No anatomical geometry synthesis, smoothing, decimation, cropping, rotation, or translation.

limitations: Display buffers are not qualified for EEG forward modeling, source localization, or AR computation.
The input is a partial example dataset containing ernie.msh, not a complete SimNIBS subject directory.
The original inferior face and neck terminate at the source model boundary; the exporter does not add missing anatomy.
The retained GM_TH_SURFACE component displays gray-matter anatomy; it is not a separately validated cortical source space or hemisphere parcellation.
Small disconnected gray-matter and internal scalp components are excluded by the documented selection rules.
Original mesh coordinates are preserved geometrically to the reported float32 rounding error; exact float64 source coordinates remain in the original .msh.

meshes.normalEncoding: Area-weighted vertex normals, signed normalized int8, divide by 127 and renormalize

selection.rule: Closed manifold connected component with maximum absolute signed volume
selection.componentLabeling: scipy.sparse.csgraph connected_components on ascending source-node compact indices

meshes.normalEncoding: Area-weighted vertex normals, signed normalized int8, divide by 127 and renormalize

selection.rule: Connected component with maximum triangle count; retain full component without hemisphere splitting
selection.componentLabeling: scipy.sparse.csgraph connected_components on ascending source-node compact indices
